title: Accuracy and precision in measurement
competency: Distinguish between accuracy and precision in measurements.

keywords.def: How close a measurement is to its accepted or known value.
How close two or more measurements are to each other.

en.text: Accuracy is how close a measurement is to the true or known value. Precision is how close repeated measurements are to each other. You can be precise but not accurate, like darts grouped together far from the bullseye.

screens.title: Darts
screens.ask: Four darts land close together, but far from the bullseye. How would you describe the throws?
screens.after: They agree with each other (precise) but miss the target (not accurate).

screens.title: Figure 1.8: three dartboards
items: All darts in the bullseye, close together: accurate and precise.
Darts close together but away from the bullseye: precise but not accurate.
Darts far apart and away from the bullseye: neither precise nor accurate.

screens.title: Accuracy and precision
paras: Accuracy is how close a measurement is to its accepted or known value.
Precision is how close two or more measurements are to each other.
Precision does not depend on accuracy.

screens.title: Key words
defs: How close a measurement is to its accepted or known value.
How close two or more measurements are to each other.

screens.title: Examples 1.7 and 1.8
steps: A substance's known mass is 10 kg. You measure 8.2 kg.
8.2 kg is not close to 10 kg, so the measurement is not accurate.
The values are close to each other, so they are precise.
But they are far from 10 kg, so they are not accurate.

screens.text: The known mass is 10 kg. Five readings are 3.2, 3.1, 3.25, 3.3 and 3.2 kg. They are
screens.why: The readings are close to each other but far from 10 kg.
screens.clue: Compare the readings with each other, then with 10 kg.

screens.text: g on Earth is 9.81 m/s². Students get 12.2, 12.3, 12.1 and 12.08 m/s². The results are
screens.why: The results are close to each other (precise) but all far from 9.81 (not accurate).

screens.text: A measurement can be accurate but not precise.
screens.why: The book says you can be accurate but not precise: readings scattered around the true value.

items: Accuracy compares with the true value.
Precision compares readings with each other.
The bullseye is the true value.
Grouped darts agree with each other.
screens.why: Accuracy is about the target; precision is about agreement.
screens.clue: Does it compare with the true value, or with other readings?

screens.text: A kitchen scale always reads 50 g too much, but it gives the same reading every time. Its readings are
screens.why: Same reading every time: precise. Always 50 g off the true value: not accurate.
screens.clue: Do the readings agree? Are they correct?
